lines.1: Quacky was a half-grown duckling when it first wandered into the Kims' countryside
lines.2: house two years ago. As Mr and Mrs Kim's two teenaged daughters were frightened of the
lines.3: duck, Mr Kim tried chasing it away several times. However, the duck was very persistent.
lines.4: It would always return, quacking softly outside if the door was closed or strolling contentedly
lines.5: all over the house if someone had forgotten to shut the door.
lines.6: After a few months of having their home invaded by the duck, Mrs Kim told her
lines.7: children that she would call a nearby animal shelter to take the duck away. However,
lines.8: despite her resolve to get their unwelcome visitor removed, she kept putting it off till a later
lines.9: date as she was very busy during that period.
lines.10: One morning, Mrs Kim was alone at home when she tripped over the edge of the
lines.11: living room rug. There was a sharp pain in her right ankle, and soon it had swollen to almost
lines.12: double its original size. That was when Mrs Kim knew she had to seek medical help quickly.
lines.13: But how? She had accidentally left her handphone in the family car the night before, and
lines.14: by the time she remembered it earlier that morning, her husband had already driven off to
lines.15: work. There was no other telephone in the house as everyone in the household relied on
lines.16: their own personal handphone. There was no way that Mrs Kim could call anyone for help.
lines.17: Fearing that she had broken her ankle, Mrs Kim was beginning to panic when she
lines.18: heard a familiar "quack, quack" coming from outside the house. Listening carefully, she
lines.19: could hear the quacking becoming louder as the duck came closer. "Quack, quack,"
lines.20: repeated the duck at frequent intervals as it approached the house. The repetitive sound
lines.21: struck Mrs Kim as comical in her dreadful situation and that strangely calmed her down.
lines.22: It so happened that the front door had not been shut properly that day, and soon a
lines.23: beak could be seen sticking out from behind the door. "Quack," went the duck happily as it
lines.25: “Oh, hello, little duck," Mrs Kim said weakly. But the moment the duck saw Mrs Kim
lines.26: lying on the floor, it quacked rapidly and hopped around flapping its wings before flying out
lines.27: of the door. Mrs Kim's heart sank at the duck's abandonment of her. Now she did not even
lines.28: have an animal to talk to as a distraction from the pain in her ankle.
lines.29: To Mrs Kim's immense surprise and relief, the duck returned several minutes later,
lines.30: followed by her neighbour, Mr Amir, who had an annoyed expression on his face. Mrs Kim
lines.31: later found out that the duck had gone to Mr Amir's house and quacked loudly and
lines.32: incessantly until Mr Amir came out of his house. The duck had somehow led him back to
lines.33: Mrs Kim. Mr Amir had intended to complain to Mrs Kim about the noisy duck, but when he
lines.34: saw what had happened to her, he quickly called for an ambulance.
lines.35: At the hospital, Mrs Kim had an X-ray which revealed that she only had an ankle
lines.36: sprain. Thanks to the prompt treatment she received, she recovered well in a couple of
lines.37: weeks. From then on, no one in the family ever spoke about getting rid of the duck again
lines.38: and the children even let it follow them about the house.
lines.39: Mrs Kim found an old basket and filled it with straw for the duck to sleep in. She also
lines.40: gave it a name that was highly meaningful to her: Quacky!

paragraphs.1: 两年前，当“嘎嘎”第一次流浪到金家的乡村小屋时，它还是一只刚长了一半大的小鸭子。由于金先生和金太太的两个十几岁的女儿都很怕这只鸭子，金先生曾多次试图把它赶走。然而，这只鸭子非常执着。如果门关着，它总会回来在外面轻声嘎嘎叫；如果有人忘了关门，它就会在屋里满足地到处溜达。
paragraphs.6: 在家里被这只鸭子“入侵”了几个月后，金太太告诉孩子们，她会打电话给附近的动物收容所把鸭子带走。然而，尽管她下定决心要赶走这位不受欢迎的访客，但由于那段时间她非常忙，便一直把这件事往后推。
paragraphs.10: 一天早上，金太太独自一人在家，不小心被客厅地毯的边缘绊倒了。她的右脚踝感到一阵剧痛，很快就肿得几乎是原来的两倍大。就在那时，金太太意识到她必须尽快寻求医疗帮助。但该怎么做呢？她前一天晚上不小心把手机忘在自家的车里了，等到那天早上她想起来时，丈夫已经开车去上班了。屋里没有其他电话，因为家里的每个人都依赖自己的私人手机。金太太根本没办法打电话向任何人求助。
paragraphs.17: 由于担心自己的脚踝骨折了，金太太开始恐慌起来。就在这时，她听到屋外面传来熟悉 的“嘎嘎，嘎嘎”声。仔细听去，随着鸭子走近，嘎嘎声越来越大。“嘎嘎，嘎嘎，”鸭子在靠近屋子时不断地重复叫着。在如此糟糕的处境下，这种重复的声音让金太太觉得很滑稽，也奇迹般地让她平静了下来。
paragraphs.22: 那天正好前门没有关好，很快就能看到一个鸭嘴从门后探了出来。“嘎嘎，”鸭子高兴地叫着走进了客厅。
paragraphs.25: “噢，你好，小鸭子，”金太太虚弱地说道。但当鸭子看到躺在地上的金太太时，它急促地嘎嘎叫了几声，拍打着翅膀在周围蹦跳，然后飞快地跑出了门。鸭子的离去让金太太的心沉了下去。现在，她连一只可以说话的动物都没有了，无法转移脚踝带来的疼痛。
paragraphs.29: 让金太太感到极其惊讶和欣慰的是，几分钟后鸭子又回来了，后面还跟着她的邻居阿米尔先生，他脸上带着恼怒的神情。金太太后来才知道，这只鸭子去了阿米尔先生家，在外面不停地大声嘎嘎叫，直到阿米尔先生从屋里走出来。这只鸭子不知怎的把他引回了金太太家。阿米尔先生原本是想来向金太太抱怨这只吵闹的鸭子的，但当他看到金太太的遭遇时，他赶紧拨打了救护车电话。
paragraphs.35: 在医院里，金太太做了X光检查，结果显示她只是脚踝扭伤。多亏了及时的治疗，她在几周内恢复得很好。从那以后，家里再也没有人提起要把鸭子送走的事了，孩子们甚至让它在屋里跟着他们到处走。
paragraphs.39: 金太太找来一个旧篮子，里面铺满稻草让鸭子睡在里面。她还给它取了一个对她来说非常有意义的名字：“嘎嘎”！
